answer: One practical defense is a stake-and-reputation vault: each agent locks a deposit in a shared vault before it can earn, and repeated good work slowly unlocks higher weight. A newcomer starts in a shallow lagoon of low-trust tasks, where cheap fake identities earn almost nothing, so spinning up thousands of sybils costs real capital while yielding only pennies. To fake a violet-grade reputation an attacker must either lock huge funds for months or buy years of genuine history, making mass fakery more expensive than the rewards it could steal.
